description: Which `process.env.NAME` reads may reach a browser bundle. The Rust bundler (`boundary::env_read_is_private`, also used by `ruvyxa_graph`) and the Node compiler (`envReadIsPrivate` in `runtime/compiler.mjs`) each decide this independently, so both replay this table. AGENTS.md already listed this policy as fixture-held; it was not, and the rule had drifted once before.
rule: A read is private unless the name is exactly NODE_ENV or begins with RUVYXA_PUBLIC_.

cases.name: NODE_ENV
cases.why: substituted at build time; the most ordinary line in a React app

cases.name: RUVYXA_PUBLIC_API_URL
cases.why: the documented browser-safe prefix

cases.name: RUVYXA_PUBLIC_
cases.why: bare prefix still carries the opt-in

cases.name: DATABASE_URL
cases.why: ordinary secret

cases.name: NODE_ENVIRONMENT
cases.why: NODE_ENV is exempt by exact match, not by prefix

cases.name: MY_NODE_ENV
cases.why: exemption is not a substring match

cases.name: node_env
cases.why: the exemption is case-sensitive

cases.name: RUVYXA_PUBLIC
cases.why: missing the trailing underscore is not the public prefix

cases.name: PREFIX_RUVYXA_PUBLIC_X
cases.why: the prefix must start the name

cases.name: ruvyxa_public_key
cases.why: the prefix is case-sensitive

cases.name: RUVYXA_SECRET
cases.why: a framework-looking name is not automatically public
an empty name is not an exemption

extraction.description: Which name a `process.env` read *is*, before the rule above classifies it. The classification table alone left this half unheld, and the two graphs disagreed: `env_read_name` in `crates/ruvyxa_bundler/src/ast.rs` reads the name with `skip_identifier`, while `parsePrivateEnvName` in `packages/ruvyxa/runtime/compiler.mjs` matched `/^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*/` — so a lower-case name was invisible to `ruvyxa dev` and refused by `ruvyxa build`, and a mixed-case name was reported under two different spellings by the two hosts. Two of the classification cases above (`node_env`, `ruvyxa_public_key`) were names the JavaScript extractor could not produce at all, so nothing tested them end to end.
extraction.rule: After `process.env`, ASCII whitespace, then either `.` immediately followed by a non-empty run of `[A-Za-z0-9_$]`, or `[` `"name"` `]` whose closing quote must follow that run directly. The run is deliberately ASCII-only and has no identifier-*start* requirement, because that is exactly what `skip_identifier` reads: `process.env["1PASSWORD_TOKEN"]` has a name and `process.env["café"]` does not.
extraction.reports: the private names only, in source order — what each host's boundary check actually acts on (`private_env_reads` in `boundary.rs`, `privateEnvReads` in `compiler.mjs`)

cases.why: the headline divergence: a lower-case name passed `dev` and was refused by `build`
a character class truncated at the first lower-case letter, so the two hosts named different variables in the same diagnostic
truncating to `NODE_ENV` made one graph read the public exemption where the other read a private name
the bracket branch is the second occurrence of the same rule; fixing only the dot branch is the classic half-fix
`$` is an identifier character, so a name that starts with one is still a name
`skip_identifier` reads continue-bytes without requiring a start byte, and a bracket access makes a leading digit legal source. `/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*/` would miss this one
makes the case-sensitivity case in the classification table above reachable from real source for the first time
the other classification case the JavaScript extractor could not produce
the whole name carries the public prefix; truncating it to `RUVYXA_PUBLIC_` happened to agree here and would not have if the prefix were shorter
the exemption, extracted whole
the run is ASCII, so it stops at the first non-ASCII byte and the read is still private under the truncated name. A Unicode identifier pattern would report `café` and diverge from Rust

the same ASCII stop leaves a non-quote character where the closing quote must be, so the bracket branch yields no name at all — the mirror of the case above, and why the two branches cannot use different patterns
a computed access has no statically-known name
whitespace before the `.` is skipped
no whitespace is skipped after the `.`, so the name run is empty and there is no read
the marker must not be preceded by an identifier character
the scanner asks the masked source, so a name inside a string is text
a template interpolation is code, and the mask says so in both graphs

importMetaEnv.description: Which module kinds get `import.meta.env` replaced by the frozen public-environment literal. The Rust compiler (`compile_module` in `crates/ruvyxa_bundler/src/compiler.rs`) and the Node compiler (`transformModuleSource` in `packages/ruvyxa/runtime/compiler.mjs`) each decide this independently, so both replay this table. The Rust half returned early for `.js`, `.mjs` and `.cjs` before the oxc transform, and the substitution lived inside that transform — so a plain-JavaScript module, an app file or any client-bundled Vite-authored dependency, reached the browser with the expression verbatim. `import.meta` carries no `env` in a browser, so the module threw `TypeError` at evaluation and killed the whole bundle rather than one expression.
importMetaEnv.rule: Every extension the bundler compiles a JavaScript module from substitutes `import.meta.env`, whichever internal path produced that module — including a `ruvyxa:` virtual entry, which the Node graph has always substituted. A mention inside a string or a comment is text and is left alone.

notCoveredHere..json: a JSON document is data; its text is never read as code
notCoveredHere..css/.scss/.sass: compiled by the style pipeline, not by the JavaScript compiler
notCoveredHere..md/.mdx: lowered to JavaScript first and then compiled as `.ts`, which this table already covers

extensions.why: plain JavaScript app code, and most shipped dependencies
what a Vite-authored dependency ships, and for the Client target `node_modules` is not external
the CommonJS spelling of the same dependency

cases.why: the Vite idiom shipped inside real dependencies; unsubstituted it throws before the guard can be false

cases.name: the whole object
cases.why: the marker is the object, not the member access after it

cases.name: a mention inside a string
cases.why: both halves ask the masked code, so text stays the text it is

cases.why: same masking rule, and a comment is not code. `markerSurvives` is not asserted: codegen drops comments, so the mention is gone entirely on every extension that is re-printed and present on every extension that is passed through
